results.extractability_reason: titolo e corpo contengono 960 caratteri: la valutazione prosegue
results.accepted_requirement: The system shall not evaluate externally-definable content as code.

iteration_history.candidate: The system shall execute shell input without evaluating content that could be defined by external sources as code.

issues: The requirement conflates two different actions: it says the system shall 'execute shell input' while also saying it shall not evaluate external content as code, which is ambiguous - it is unclear whether execution of shell input is asserted as a guarantee or merely as context for the prohibition.

The evidence only names the file scrapy/shell.py where eval() was found; it does not describe what 'shell input' means, how it flows into eval(), or that the fix concerns command execution as opposed to some other evaluated content.
revision_instructions: Rewrite as a single, unambiguous prohibition rather than combining an 'execute' action with a 'without evaluating' clause.

Remove or justify the specific framing of 'shell input': the evidence gives only a file name, not a description of what content is evaluated or how it originates; state the prohibition at the general level the evidence supports, i.e. that externally-definable content must not be evaluated as code.

iteration_history.candidate: The system shall not evaluate externally-definable content as code.

issues: This states the same behaviour class as the security-fix pattern accepted for similar eval()-based vulnerabilities in other PRs, if such exist in the project history.

results.title: Fix: Unsafe XML Processing Library Could Allow Malicious Attacks in scrapy/http/request/rpc.py
results.extractability_reason: titolo e corpo contengono 852 caratteri: la valutazione prosegue

iteration_history.candidate: When processing XML-RPC request data, the system shall not be vulnerable to malicious XML content such as entity expansion or external entity attacks.

retrieved_requirements.statement: The system shall not evaluate externally-definable content as code.
The system shall prevent untrusted input from causing arbitrary code to be loaded and executed when importing modules.
The system shall prevent untrusted input from causing arbitrary code modules to be loaded and executed during spider generation.
The system shall export data without executing code contained in the serialized data being processed.

issues: The evidence states only that xmlrpc 'is not inherently safe from vulnerabilities' and that defusedxml.xmlrpc should be used instead; it does not name entity expansion or external entity attacks specifically.
The specific attack types in the candidate appear to be drawn from general knowledge of what defusedxml protects against, not from the text of the evidence.
revision_instructions: Remove the specific attack types 'entity expansion' and 'external entity attacks': the evidence only refers generically to 'vulnerabilities' associated with xmlrpc, without naming these attack classes.

State the requirement at the level of generality the evidence supports, e.g. that malicious XML content must not compromise the system when XML-RPC request data is processed, without enumerating specific attack mechanisms not mentioned in the evidence.

iteration_history.candidate: When processing XML-RPC request data, the system shall not be exposed to security vulnerabilities arising from malicious XML content.

retrieved_requirements.statement: The system shall not evaluate externally-definable content as code.
The system shall prevent untrusted input from causing arbitrary code to be loaded and executed when importing modules.
The system shall prevent untrusted input from causing arbitrary code modules to be loaded and executed during spider generation.
The system shall export data without executing code contained in the serialized data being processed.

issues: The requirement states an abstract security quality ('not be exposed to security vulnerabilities arising from malicious XML content') rather than an observable behaviour; this is analogous to 'the code must be secure', which the black-box test explicitly excludes.

The evidence itself only says xmlrpc 'is not inherently safe from vulnerabilities' and recommends defusedxml.xmlrpc instead, without stating any concrete effect (e.g., what happens to entity expansion, external references, denial of service, or code execution) that an observer could check before and after the change.

This is the second attempt at generalizing the requirement; the first was rejected for naming specific attack types not in the evidence, and this version, having removed them, is left with no testable content at all, indicating the evidence does not support a checkable requirement at any level of generality between these two extremes.
unsupported_claims: not be exposed to security vulnerabilities (no concrete, observable effect stated)

iteration_history.candidate: If a source file imports a module that transitively imports twisted.internet.reactor outside the approved entry points, then the system shall fail the import-check with an error identifying the disallowed import.

issues: The evidence states only that a pre-existing 'banned imports' mechanism (from PR #6941) has been extended to cover more modules that import twisted.internet.reactor; it gives no detail about how the ban is enforced, what observable effect it produces, or what constitutes an 'approved entry point'.

The candidate invents mechanism-level specifics -- 'transitively imports', 'approved entry points', 'fail the import-check with an error identifying the disallowed import' -- none of which appear in the evidence; these read as plausible detail from familiarity with import-linting tools rather than from the text.

The evidence does not establish that this is a runtime, externally observable behaviour of the deployed system at all; it reads as an internal source-tree/test-suite restriction (a rollback and extension of an import ban list), which is closer to internal tooling than to a caller-visible guarantee.

Removing the unsupported specifics leaves at most 'the system bans some imports that import twisted.internet.reactor', which restates the title without adding any grounded, checkable behaviour beyond what is already just an assertion that a change was made.
